communities.historical_geography: Rhineland, France, Germany, Poland, Lithuania, Russia, Central/Eastern Europe, Anglo-American diaspora
communities.halakhic_decisors: Moses Isserles (Rema), Vilna Gaon, Chafetz Chaim (Yisrael Meir Kagan), Moshe Feinstein
communities.historical_heritage: Flourishing of Franco-German Tosafist commentary and Eastern European Yeshivish and Hasidic traditions.

communities.historical_geography: Iberian Peninsula (Spain & Portugal) prior to 1492; Ottoman Empire, Balkans, North Africa, Western Europe (Amsterdam, London, Livorno)
communities.language: Ladino / Judezmo (Judeo-Spanish), Western Sephardi Portuguese/Spanish, Rabbinic Hebrew
communities.halakhic_decisors: Joseph Karo (Maran), Chida (Rabbi Hayyim Yosef David Azulai), Ben Ish Chai, Rabbi Ovadia Yosef
communities.historical_heritage: Classical Judeo-Spanish Golden Age, philosophical synthesis, and systematic codification (Shulchan Aruch).

sub_traditions.name: Western Sephardim (Spanish and Portuguese Jews)
sub_traditions.centers: Amsterdam, London, Hamburg, Bayonne, New York, Philadelphia, Curaçao
sub_traditions.character: Western civic acculturation, stately choral liturgy (Minhag Amsterdam), distinguished communal discipline (Nação), authorities including Menasseh ben Israel, Jacob Sasportas, David Nieto

sub_traditions.name: Eastern Sephardim (Ottoman Sephardim)
sub_traditions.centers: Salonika, Istanbul, Izmir, Rhodes, Sarajevo, Sofia, Jerusalem
sub_traditions.character: Vibrant Ladino-speaking culture, preservation of medieval Spanish ballads (romanceros), halakhic flourishing under authorities such as Rabbi Joseph Karo and Rabbi Hayyim Palachi

communities.historical_geography: Middle East, Mesopotamia (Iraq/Babylon), Persia/Iran, Syria, Lebanon, Central Asia
communities.heritage: Direct heirs of the ancient Babylonian academies of Sura and Pumbedita and Persian-era exilic communities
communities.halakhic_decisors: Geonim (Saadia Gaon, Hai Gaon), Ben Ish Hai (Rabbi Yosef Hayyim of Baghdad), Abdullah Somekh, Rabbi Ezra Attiya

sub_traditions.name: Iraqi / Babylonian Jewry
sub_traditions.character: Unbroken 2,500-year continuity from Babylonian exile; premier halakhic authority in Ben Ish Hai integrating halakha with Lurianic Kabbalah; Midrash Ben Ish Hai; distinctive Aramaic/Arabic liturgical melodies

sub_traditions.name: Persian / Iranian Jewry
sub_traditions.centers: Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz, Yazd, Hamedan, Bukhara, Mountain Jews of the Caucasus
sub_traditions.character: Ancient community tracing origins to Cyrus the Great and Book of Esther; rich Judeo-Persian literature (Shahin Shirazi epics), distinct Passover customs, and veneration of tombs of Esther, Mordecai, and Daniel

sub_traditions.name: Syrian Jewry (Shami)
sub_traditions.character: Custodians of the 10th-century Aleppo Codex (Keter Aram Tzova); legendary Maqam-based Pizmonim tradition; famous 1935 Rabbinic Edict strictly forbidding acceptance of converts to protect communal cohesion

communities.halakhic_decisors: Isaac Alfasi (Rif), Raphael Berdugo, Shalom Messas, Israel Abuhatzeira (Baba Sali)
distinctive_practices: Veneration of tzaddikim and joyful Hilula anniversary pilgrimages
Celebration of Mimouna at the conclusion of Passover celebrating springtime and communal friendship
Ancient rabbinic courts of Fes and Meknes with distinct halakhic ordinances (Takkanot of Castile and Fes)

communities.language: Judeo-Yemenite Arabic, ancient Yemenite Hebrew with archaic Babylonian vocalization and phonetic preservation of letters (gimel, dalet, vav, tet, ayin, qof)
communities.halakhic_decisors: Moses ben Maimon (Maimonides / Rambam - author of Iggeret Teiman), Rabbi Shalom Sharabi, Rabbi Yihyeh Qafih

sub_streams.name: Baladi (Traditional/Native)
sub_streams.description: Follows Maimonides' Mishneh Torah almost exclusively as the sole decisor; maintains the ancient pre-Kabbalistic Tiklal prayer book without later mystical accretions; recites Targum Aramaic verse-by-verse during Torah reading

sub_streams.name: Shami (Levantine/Sephardic)
sub_streams.description: Adopted the Sephardic Shulchan Aruch and Lurianic Kabbalah starting in the 17th century following the arrival of printed books from Safed and Salonika

sub_streams.name: Dor Deah (Dardaim)
sub_streams.description: Rationalist reform movement founded in early 20th-century Sanaa by Rabbi Yihyeh Qafih, rejecting the Zohar and Kabbalistic theology in favor of pure Maimonidean rationalism, fiercely opposed by the traditionalist Iqshim

communities.historical_geography: Gondar, Simien Mountains, Tigray (northwestern Ethiopia), modern State of Israel
communities.language: Ge'ez (classical liturgical language), Amharic, Tigrinya, Modern Hebrew
communities.scripture: The Orit (Octateuch in Ge'ez: Pentateuch plus Joshua, Judges, Ruth) alongside Ge'ez Enoch, Jubilees, and Testament of Abraham
communities.religious_tradition: Haymanot (pre-rabbinic, non-talmudic biblical Judaism preserved in isolation for centuries)
communities.leadership_structure: Kessim / Kohanim (spiritual leaders and priestly sacrificers wearing white turbans) and an ancient monastic order (founded by monks such as Abba Sabra in the 15th century)
communities.liturgy_and_prayer: Sung prayers in Ge'ez and Agaw (Qwarinya) accompanied by liturgical drums (kebero) and prayer sticks in the Masgid (prayer house)
distinctive_practices: Rigorous biblical purity laws (attinkun: ritual isolation of menstruating women in ya-margam gogo huts and mothers after childbirth in ya-dass gogo, followed by total river immersion)
Strict Sabbath observance (Sanbat personified as heavenly queen and bride, forbidding fire, cooking, or leaving village)
Unique festival of Seged (celebrated 29th of Heshvan, 50 days after Yom Kippur, climbing a mountain with stones to renew the Sinaitic covenant as in Ezra-Nehemiah)
communities.relationship_to_rabbinic_judaism: Historically isolated from the Talmud and rabbinic halakhic developments; halakhically recognized in 16th century by Rabbi David ben Zimra (Radbaz) as originating from the lost Tribe of Dan; definitively recognized in 1973 by Sephardic Chief Rabbi Ovadia Yosef; integrated into modern Israel through Operation Moses (1984) and Operation Solomon (1991), followed by institutional dialogue over rabbinic marriage and recognition of Kessim.
communities.uniqueness: Preserved pre-rabbinic, non-talmudic biblical Judaism with monastic priesthood (Kohanim/Kessim) until mass airlift migrations to Israel (Operation Moses 1984, Operation Solomon 1991)

communities.historical_geography: Iran (Hamadan, Isfahan, Shiraz, Tehran, Kashan, Yazd), Central Asia, contemporary diaspora (Los Angeles, New York, Tel Aviv)
communities.language: Judeo-Persian dialects, Judeo-Tat, Judeo-Tajik (Bukhori), Persian, Hebrew
communities.liturgical_rite: Nusach Paras / Nusach Edot Ha-Mizrach with archaic Babylonian and Persian cantillations
communities.halakhic_decisors: Babylonian Geonim, Mullahs and Hakhamim of Isfahan and Hamadan (Hakham Yedidia Shofet, Hakham Uriel Davidi)
communities.historical_heritage: One of the oldest diaspora communities dating 2,700 years to the Assyrian and Babylonian exiles; received the Edict of Cyrus the Great (538 BCE); preserves the pilgrimage tombs of Queen Esther and Mordecai in Hamadan, the Prophet Daniel in Susa, and Habakkuk in Tuyserkan; rich tradition of Judeo-Persian epic poetry (Shahin Shirazi, Imrani).
distinctive_practices: Veneration and annual pilgrimage to the Mausoleum of Esther and Mordecai in Hamadan on Purim
Unique Passover Seder ritual using scallions/leeks during Dayenu symbolizing the whips of Egyptian taskmasters
Celebration of Rooz-e Baghi and integration of Persian cultural milestones with strict halakhic observance

communities.historical_geography: Mesopotamia / Iraq (Baghdad, Basra, Mosul, Hillah, Kurdistan), Anglo-Indian Sassoon diaspora, contemporary Israel
communities.language: Judeo-Arabic (Baghdadi dialect), Judeo-Aramaic (Kurdistani Neo-Aramaic), Rabbinic Hebrew
communities.liturgical_rite: Nusach Baghdad (Edot Ha-Mizrach) with strict Iraqi Maqamat system for Pizmonim and liturgical poetry
communities.halakhic_decisors: Babylonian Geonim (Saadia Gaon, Sherira Gaon, Hai Gaon), Rabbi Abdallah Somekh (Midrash Beit Zilkha), Rabbi Yosef Hayyim (Ben Ish Hai)
communities.historical_heritage: Direct unbroken 2,500-year continuity from the Babylonian exile (586 BCE); historical redactors and custodians of the Babylonian Talmud in the academies of Sura, Pumbedita, and Nehardea under the Exilarch (Resh Galuta); premier halakhic synthesizing tradition integrating legal codification with Lurianic Kabbalah.
distinctive_practices: Uncompromising fidelity to the halakhic and kabbalistic rulings of the Ben Ish Hai
Rich liturgical Pizmonim tradition following the classical Arabic Maqam system pegged to the weekly Torah reading
Pilgrimages to the shrines of the Prophet Ezekiel (Al-Kifl), Ezra the Scribe (Al-Uzair), and Joshua the High Priest (Baghdad)
